A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 18 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original online-learning experiments, scalability analyses, FPGA synthesis and post-route validation results, including extended baseline experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental and hardware-analysis results in Sections 5–6 and Appendices B–D.

M1.justification: The LUT-based spline evaluation, sparse coefficient updates, gradient propagation and streaming learning procedures remain unchanged. Revised spline-order symbols and newly stated analytical omissions do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate drifting function approximation, rotating XOR qubit readout, randomized Acrobot control and handwritten-digit classification with angular drift. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: MLP-P/L, actor-critic MLPs, MLP-DQN, OS-ELM, the frozen digit learner and Appendix D's LSUV/LayerNorm variants participate in the same comparisons.

E3.justification: Training rules, architectures, bitwidths, learning rates, task streams, metrics and hardware validation procedures are retained. Table 2 removes the repeated target-clock column, but its caption still specifies the same 5 ns constraint.

E4.justification: The precision and capacity sweeps, decision-boundary example, input-dimension scaling analysis and initialization/normalization studies remain unchanged in Figures 4–7 and 10 and Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both versions report Acrobot returns as mean ± standard deviation over random seeds and retain Appendix C.3's fixed-seed statement. No run counts, uncertainty practices or statistical procedures change.

E6.justification: The empirical values, plotted findings and result entries are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains 92.8% KAN qubit-readout accuracy, and Table 2 retains online-update latencies of 50, 140 and 70 ns. Appendix D's results also match.

T1.justification: The update-cost ratio changes from s/(G+s), with s=p+1, to (S+1)/(G+S), with S denoting spline order. The locality lemma changes 'at most' to 'exactly,' and Appendix A.1 replaces corresponding inequalities with equalities. v3 also removes the saturated-quantization definition and explicitly states analytical omissions of biases and base activations. The remaining bounds and proof arguments are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about sparse updates, capacity scaling, fixed-point robustness and the first demonstration of model-free online learning at sub-microsecond latencies.

C2.justification: Section 3 newly asserts that omitting MLP biases and KAN base activations does not affect complexity or boundedness because the same structural arguments apply. Experimental interpretations and the substantive limitations in Section 7 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Removing Definition 3.1 also removes the explicit explanation that W and I denote total and integer precision, although tables still use this notation. Concrete formats, rounding/saturation modes, build instructions, FPGA specifications and stream-generation details remain documented.

R1.justification: KANELÉ receives updated publication metadata. The added main-text LSUV citation refers to the work already cited in Appendix D, now duplicated as 2016a/2016b. Neither the set of distinct cited works nor research positioning changes.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes much of the mathematical notation, removes the separate preliminaries heading, relabels theorems as propositions and updates cross-references and appendix headings. The publication footer changes to conference proceedings information; most prose and section ordering remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 uses larger, clearer text and simplified headers after removing its redundant clock column. Figure 10 moves between columns, other material reflows, and captions receive limited edits. All ten figures and five tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The revised G+S coefficient count agrees with Table 1 and Appendix B, and Table 2 becomes easier to read. However, the locality lemma and Appendix A.1 strengthen upper bounds into exact nonzero counts without additional conditions explaining that stronger assertion, while the explicit quantization definition disappears. With empirical evidence unchanged, these clarity gains and concerns about mathematical qualification leave the net quality effect uncertain.
